scope: Read actual static/trajectory source, full validator and partial-capture addition, current and historical reports, preparation/input outline, assessment and closest archived AUTHOR. Checked all frozen payload hashes. No scientific execution, author-source modification or model trial by this reviewer.

findings.detail: The scaling q=sqrt(s)*x and p=s*P gives H=s^2*h and closed-orbit area proportional to s^(3/2). The cubic stationary-point equation, saddle factorization and lobe-area integrand are correct. Both lobes grow monotonically and the saddle remains nondegenerate. Their growth-rate fractions equal their fixed area fractions; the outgoing branch action equals that fraction of the incoming action at capture.

findings.topic: Initial preparation and order of limits
findings.detail: The initial energy inversion fixes the declared action. Uniform time points over the frozen periodic orbit are uniform canonical angle, not uniform polar angle. Gauss action weights normalized by the band width and equally weighted phase points implement the stated finite-width ensemble. The input averages this ensemble at finite duration before taking duration to infinity and keeps a classical isolated Hamiltonian throughout. No single-trajectory or zero-width limit is substituted.

The global-volume source computes one common energy from the full phase volume and is exactly shared on connected outer trajectories. After splitting into disconnected lobes it continues an ergodic volume rule, whereas the physical population retains separate branch actions and energies. This is a physical adiabatic-ensemble approximation, not an action-factor bug or an intentionally failed integrator. The related collisionless-trap archive concerns noncrossing mode actions and a common thermal state; the shared adiabatic theme is explicitly disclosed.

Direct Hamiltonian propagation uses no final capture fractions or branch-action substitutions. Initial area inversion is shared only to instantiate the physical preparation. The fourth-order extended-space splitting advances q and time around potential kicks and accumulates the correct explicit-control work. Separate adaptive DOP853 propagation checks integration, while final energy is evaluated directly from q,p. This is independent dynamical evidence for the static capture rule; it is not an analytic proof of the infinite-duration numerical error.

All candidate calibration endpoints remain outside capture for the entire action range, so source and physical predictions agree exactly. With J=J0*z and a fixed uniform z distribution, d<E>/dJ0=<z*omega(J0*z)> is strictly positive since each calibration orbit has positive frequency. Thus global identification follows analytically; the nine control profiles and seventeen successful inverse fits corroborate it rather than replace the argument.

The report separates time step, duration, action/phase resolution, phase offset and ramp-shape checks. Error is correctly allowed to be nonmonotone with duration at fixed phase grid. The captured-domain energy magnitudes exceed .845 and the 27-point minimum source gap is .0965, so the intended signal is not manufactured by a near-zero energy denominator. This prototype does not establish a complete graded domain, 256-noise fit margin or task runtime.

The original s_final=.45 case was labeled partial capture but is genuinely noncrossing. Original source/report/logs remain byte-preserved. The final report relabels it and adds s_final=.48859552155 with exactly half the action band captured. Splitting the action quadrature at the threshold gives the correct finite-width measure. The old 27 fully captured predictions change by at most6.7e-16; no original trajectory was discarded or rerun. The new small-energy case is correctly limited to validation rather than proposed scored separation.

The outline supplies the entire controlled Hamiltonian and fixed energy zero, classical unit mass, action and orbital-time preparation, known monotone ramp, isolation, final position/momentum energy measurement and ensemble-before-duration limit. These determine the readout. It does not supply capture probabilities, branch actions, phase-volume repair or a solver mandate. A future package still needs its API, fixed instrument sigma, full-domain control checks and ordinary unrestricted instruction.

primary_source_checked.title: Averaging method for systems with separatrix crossing
primary_source_checked.author: Anatoly Neishtadt
primary_source_checked.support: Canonical-angle averaging, nondegenerate separatrix with positive capture integrals, growth-rate capture probabilities and action/area derivative identities support this homothetic classical construction.

qualifications: Approval is for a bounded scientific prototype only. No task, grader, calibration-noise dataset, local controls or measured model failure is approved by this report.
Numerical convergence is empirical and materially below the proposed .04 scale in checked cases; it is not a uniform theorem over every continuous endpoint.
A future agent that recognizes capture but miscodes branch, angle, action or integration formulas must be classified separately from a retained global-volume physical closure.
